summary: A bare return from a JS function produces the undefined value; it is not equivalent to C# void when the call result is observable.

target.notes: Functions that fall off the end also return undefined. Use void only when whole-program analysis proves the result is never observed and function identity/calling convention allows it.

caveats: C# null is not JavaScript undefined.
references: ECMAScript 2026 Language Specification Return Statement Runtime Semantics
